content.user_title: Turn Design Corrections Into Reusable Rules
content.value_statement: Design corrections are easily lost between agent sessions. This skill converts your feedback into proposed rules with reasons and writes only approved changes.
actual_capabilities: Collect explicit corrections, user edits, repeated feedback, rejections, and confirmed design choices from accessible sessions.
Filter one-off changes and compare reusable corrections against existing project rules.
Propose narrowly scoped rules with source evidence and clearly marked inferred reasons.
Identify conflicts, ask clarification questions, and recommend automated checks for detectable violations.
Write approved rules to project design guidance or project skills and show the resulting diff.
Implement approved checks or propose pruning duplicate, contradictory, and vague rules.
limitations: Requires explicit invocation and user approval before writing proposed changes.
Earlier session analysis depends on accessible transcripts and the sessions the user requests.
Does not change component code or fix existing violations without separate permission.
Cannot establish unstated design preferences or confirm inferred reasons without user input.

use_cases.title: Preserve Product Design Decisions
use_cases.description: Convert repeated visual corrections into specific project rules with confirmed reasons.

use_cases.title: Enforce Repeated UI Constraints
use_cases.description: Identify design corrections that can become approved lint rules, token restrictions, or tests.

use_cases.title: Maintain Shared Agent Guidance
use_cases.description: Review accumulated design rules and propose merges, conflict resolutions, and clearer wording.
use_cases.target_user: Design system maintainers managing project guidance

prompt_templates.title: Review This Session
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: collect current-session design corrections and stop at the proposal report.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Recent Sessions
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: review the three most recent accessible sessions for reusable design corrections.

prompt_templates.title: Approve Selected Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Write 1, 3 from the last report. Use the reasons I confirmed and leave unresolved items unchanged.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: persist only selected proposals after reviewing the report and answering clarification questions.

prompt_templates.title: Prune Existing Guidance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: propose duplicate merges, contradiction fixes, and stricter wording in existing design guidance before writing.

output_examples.input: I corrected raised surfaces to use shadow-raised instead of borders because borders make them look flat.
output: Rules to add: Raised surfaces use shadow-raised instead of solid borders.
Why: Borders make raised surfaces look flat.
Where: Project design guidance, Surfaces section.
Needs your answer: Confirm whether this rule covers cards, popovers, and menus.

output_examples.input: I changed dropdown duration from 400ms to 200ms but did not explain why.
output: Rules to add: Dropdowns open in 200ms.
Why, inferred: The previous duration felt too slow.
Needs your answer: Is that reason correct, and should this also apply to popovers?
Make it a check: Consider an approved duration-token restriction.

output_examples.input: Review this session, which only contains a functional bug fix and a one-page headline change.
output_examples.output: No reusable design corrections found in this session.

best_practices: Review each source quote or edit before approving a generalized rule.
Confirm inferred reasons and resolve conflicts before writing guidance.
Keep rules narrowly scoped and prefer approved automated checks for detectable violations.
anti_patterns: Turning one-page content changes or functional bug fixes into general design rules.
Writing inferred reasons as facts without user confirmation.
Applying a project preference globally or fixing component violations without permission.

faq.question: Does this skill run automatically?
faq.answer: No. The source requires explicit invocation and disables model invocation.

faq.question: Can it review earlier sessions?
faq.answer: Yes, when you request those sessions and their transcripts are accessible. Claude Code transcripts may be stored in its local project directory.

faq.question: Does it write rules immediately?
faq.answer: No. It presents proposals and questions, then waits for approval. You can approve all items or select specific ones.

faq.question: Where does it store approved rules?
faq.answer: It normally uses project DESIGN.md. It may propose project skills, automated checks, or a pointer from existing agent guidance.

faq.question: What happens when my reason is missing?
faq.answer: It marks a proposed reason as inferred and asks you to confirm it before writing.

faq.question: Will it fix code that violates a new check?
faq.answer: It runs approved checks and reports existing violations. Component fixes require separate permission.
